title: Female Reproductive System Anatomy: Ovaries & Fallopian
description: Learn female reproductive system anatomy across the ovaries, uterine tubes, uterus, cervix, vaginal canal, pelvic support ligaments, and external openings.
h1: Female Reproductive System Anatomy: Ovaries, Uterus and Tract
blurb: Cyclic follicle maturation in the ovaries, ciliary transport along the uterine tubes, a hormonally dynamic uterus and cervix, vaginal canal, and external vulva.
lead: Spanning the true pelvis and perineum, the female reproductive system coordinates cyclic egg maturation, fertilization transport, pregnancy support, and childbirth. In this illustrated guide to female reproductive system anatomy, we examine 20 documented structures—including fundus & body, endometrium, cervix, vagina—linking regional topography, tissue architecture, physiological mechanisms, and clinical reasoning.
overview: Spanning the true pelvis and perineum, the female reproductive system coordinates cyclic egg maturation, fertilization transport, pregnancy support, and childbirth. Each cycle, FSH recruits a follicle that secretes oestradiol and builds the endometrium; the LH surge triggers ovulation at a variable cycle day (often about 14 days before the next period), and the corpus luteum then secretes progesterone to make the endometrium secretory. If fertilisation does not occur the corpus luteum regresses, progesterone falls and menstruation follows. Fertilisation normally happens in the ampulla of the uterine tube, and the embryo reaches the uterus after 3–4 days. The cervix, with its mucus plug, and the vaginal microbiome form the defence against ascending infection. Within the human body, the female reproductive system (Organa genitalia feminina) is situated in pelvis: uterus, tubes, ovaries, vagina, receives arterial perfusion via uterine + ovarian arteries (internal iliac & aorta), and is innervated by uterovaginal plexus (T12–L2 sympathetic, S2–S4 parasympathetic).

The fundus & body (Fundus et corpus uteri) is the domed fundus above the tubal openings and the tapering body, of smooth muscle (myometrium) lined by endometrium. Physiologically, the fundus & body houses and nourishes a pregnancy; the myometrium generates labour. The endometrium is a functional layer of glands and stroma that proliferates under oestrogen and becomes secretory under progesterone, plus a permanent basal layer. Physiologically, the endometrium governs site of implantation; sheds each cycle if no embryo implants. The cervix (Cervix uteri) is the fibrous neck projecting into the vagina, with an endocervical canal of mucus-secreting columnar epithelium and a squamous ectocervix. Physiologically, the cervix keeps pregnancy in and microbes out; dilates 10 cm in labour. The vagina is a fibromuscular canal lined by glycogen-rich stratified squamous epithelium, angled back over the levator plate. Physiologically, the vagina governs birth canal, menstrual outlet and copulatory organ; lactobacilli keep pH ~4. The uterine tube (Tuba uterina) is a 10 cm ciliated duct with interstitial, isthmic, ampullary and infundibular parts. Physiologically, the uterine tube governs captures the oocyte, is the site of fertilisation (ampulla) and transports the embryo by ciliary beat and peristalsis. Structurally, the fimbriae (Fimbriae tubae) comprises finger-like projections around the tubal opening, one (fimbria ovarica) attached to the ovary. Physiologically, the fimbriae governs sweep the oocyte into the tube at ovulation.

Clinically, regarding the fundus & body, fibroids (leiomyomas) arise in the myometrium and cause heavy bleeding and pressure symptoms. From a diagnostic standpoint, in the endometrium, ectopic endometrium (endometriosis) causes cyclical pain and infertility; unopposed oestrogen drives hyperplasia and carcinoma. In clinical pathology involving the cervix, the squamocolumnar junction is where cervical cancer begins — the target of smear tests and HPV vaccination. Medical evaluation of the vagina also notes that the acidic pH protects against infection; antibiotics and oestrogen loss can allow candidiasis.

questions.question: What organs are included in the female reproductive system?
questions.answer: The system includes ovaries, uterine tubes, uterus, cervix, vagina and external genital structures. Each has distinct roles in cycles, reproduction and pelvic support. Structurally, the broad & suspensory ligaments (Ligamentum latum) comprises peritoneal folds (broad, round, ovarian, suspensory) carrying the tubes, vessels and ureters. Physiologically, the broad & suspensory ligaments governs suspend the uterus and convey its vessels.

questions.question: Where does fertilization usually occur?
questions.answer: Fertilization most often occurs in the ampulla of a uterine tube. The resulting early embryo travels toward the uterine cavity. The uterine tube (Tuba uterina) is a 10 cm ciliated duct with interstitial, isthmic, ampullary and infundibular parts. Physiologically, the uterine tube governs captures the oocyte, is the site of fertilisation (ampulla) and transports the embryo by ciliary beat and peristalsis.
